summary: Adaptive batcher linger accumulation causing sustained p95/p99 latency plateaus and intermittent 504s
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports sustained p95/p99 latency plateaus and intermittent 504s for a subset of inference routes since 2026-03-12 08:10 UTC. Symptoms correlate with low-to-moderate QPS bursts (5-30 qps per connection) and heavy use of streaming responses.

Impact:
- Several production endpoints for BlinkAI (dedicated tenant) experienced p95 increases from ~180ms to ~1.1s and p99 from ~350ms to ~2.4s for an 18-hour window.
- Intermittent 504s observed at the API gateway for long-running streaming calls (~0.6% error rate during peak).
- Customer-facing features (real-time summarization) degraded; customer requesting urgent mitigation.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity pool: dc-dedicated-us-east-3
- Serving runtime v2.14.1, batcher subsystem v1.9.0 (adaptive linger enabled), api-gateway v3.2.0
- Models: redwood-open-7b-quant pinned to v2026-02-28

Steps to reproduce (customer flow):
1. Open a streaming chat session from BlinkAI web client.
2. Send short prompts (avg 12 tokens) at variable inter-message intervals (200ms-800ms).
3. Observe backend metrics and API latency.

Observed behavior:
- Continuous/adaptive batcher linger time grows over time under the above workload pattern, causing larger microbatches and delayed flushes.
- p95/p99 latency plateaus and sporadic 504s map to batch flush events where queue dwell exceeds expected thresholds.

Expected behavior:
- Linger adapts to maintain latency SLOs; short prompt workloads should not accumulate linger such that p99 crosses 2s.

Useful links / logs:
- Grafana panels: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/Serving/latency-overview?orgId=1&var-tenant=BlinkAI
- Trace: https://tracing.redwood.ai/trace/abcdef123456
- API gateway logs (sample): logs/gateway/BlinkAI-20260312-08.log

investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 09:00 UTC - Observed that linger timer (adaptive-batcher.linger_ms) starts at 2ms but climbs to >40ms after sustained low-amplitude bursts on a per-connection basis.
2026-03-12 09:20 UTC - Correlated batch size spikes with p99 spikes; traces show single-connection microbatches holding multiple short requests rather than flushing quickly.
2026-03-12 10:10 UTC - Hypothesis 1: Adaptive linger algorithm scales linger based on recent batch fill-rate but fails to decay quickly when QPS oscillates, creating 'linger accumulation'.

2026-03-12 10:40 UTC - Hypothesis 2: KV-cache warmup for quantized model on dedicated pool can add per-batch setup time; when combined with larger microbatches this increases tail latency and occasionally exceeds gateway timeout windows.
2026-03-12 11:45 UTC - Tested repro by replaying customer traffic on staging with adaptive linger enabled; reproduced p99 plateau when inter-message jitter matched production pattern.
2026-03-13 01:30 UTC - Experiment: Disabled adaptive scaling and set fixed linger to 6ms on a canary host. p95 reduced and p99 tail improved, but throughput dropped 3%.
2026-03-13 04:00 UTC - Metric snapshots: batcher.dwell_ms median rose from 1.8ms to 18.4ms; batcher.batch_size median rose from 1.3 to 4.9 for affected routes.

2026-03-13 08:50 UTC - Found code path where adaptive decay factor uses an integer division in corner cases leading to slower decay when QPS < 10 per-connection. See PR reference in related_github_prs.
2026-03-14 07:30 UTC - Deployed temporary config change (upper bound on linger and faster decay constant) to BlinkAI's dedicated pool; partial mitigation confirmed.
2026-03-14 08:00 UTC - Noted a secondary improvement after warming KV caches via prefetch for pinned model; reduced per-batch setup jitter.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied 2026-03-14 07:30 UTC: lowered adaptive linger upper cap to 12ms and increased decay rate for per-connection linger to avoid accumulation.
Customer impact: p99 reduced from ~2.4s to ~480ms; 504s dropped from ~0.6% to <0.05% for BlinkAI routes.

Root cause: adaptive linger algorithm had an incorrect decay calculation for low-QPS per-connection traffic, allowing linger to grow and persist across oscillations. Secondary contributor: KV-cache warmup increased per-batch overhead which amplified tail.

Permanent fix: engineering to merge PR that corrects decay math and adds unit tests for low-QPS hysteresis (target: patch release v1.9.1). Follow-up tasks include a canary rollout and adding an alert on batcher.dwell_ms > 15ms for >5m.
Follow-ups assigned: INT-4021 (add batcher low-QPS unit tests), INT-4078 (telemetry: per-tenant linger histograms), SUP-73659 (customer follow-up: confirm long-term stability).
Customer communication: sent summary and mitigation notes to BlinkAI on 2026-03-14 09:30 UTC; scheduling a technical review with their SRE for 2026-03-18.
Postmortem: link pending to Confluence page; will include timeline, graphing of dwell_ms, and recommendation to include adaptive linger upper caps for dedicated pools.

Rollout notes: Patch v1.9.1 will be rolled to staging canary 2026-03-16, gradual production rollout 2026-03-17 to 2026-03-18 with per-tenant safeguards and automated rollback on increased error rates.
